note.explanation: A solution is unsaturated if it can still dissolve more solute at a particular temperature. It is saturated when the maximum amount of solute has dissolved in a particular amount of solvent at that temperature. Different solutes can dissolve in different amounts.
note.checkAnswer: A saturated solution: no more solute dissolves at that temperature.
note.simple: Unsaturated means there is still room for more solute to dissolve. Saturated means the solution has dissolved as much solute as it can at that temperature.
note.checkQuestion: What happens to extra sugar added to a saturated solution?
note.title: Unsaturated and saturated solutions
steps: Add a small amount of sugar to water and stir; it dissolves.
Keep adding and stirring; sugar continues to dissolve while the solution can take more.
When no more sugar dissolves, the solution is saturated at that temperature.
At 20°C, 100 g of water dissolves 36 g of sodium chloride or 203.9 g of table sugar to form saturated solutions.
note.answer: The extra sugar does not dissolve and settles at the bottom.

written.text: Define solubility of a solute. How does the solubility of solutes change with the increase in temperature?
written.finalAnswer: Solubility is the amount of a solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature. For most solid solutes, solubility increases as temperature increases, but the change depends on the solute.

explain.title: Unsaturated solution
explain.body: A solution which can dissolve more amount of a solute at a particular temperature is called an unsaturated solution. So, if more sugar can still dissolve, the solution is unsaturated.

explain.title: Saturated solution
explain.body: A solution in which the maximum amount of the solute has been dissolved in a particular amount of a solvent at a particular temperature is called a saturated solution. Any extra sugar added at this stage will not dissolve and will settle at the bottom.

explain.title: Solubilities can differ
explain.body: Different solutes have different solubilities in a particular solvent. At 20°C, 36 g of sodium chloride or 203.9 g of table sugar can dissolve in 100 g of water to make saturated solutions.

explain.title: Why sugar dissolves in a larger amount
explain.body: The section explains that sugar molecules are larger than salt ions. More water molecules can surround a single sugar molecule, causing sugar to dissolve in larger amounts.

mistakes: Calling a solution saturated just because it contains some dissolved solute; it is saturated only when the maximum amount has dissolved at that temperature.
Leaving out the particular temperature when defining saturated or unsaturated solutions.
Mixing up solute and solvent: sugar or salt is the solute, and water is the solvent.
Comparing solubilities without keeping the amount of water and temperature the same.
